UPDATE 2026-11-14 (breakpoint storage, dark behind EDITOR_CANVAS): BlockNode (lib/entity-blocks/node-tree.ts) gains an optional, additive `responsive?: { tablet?, phone? }` of sparse content-field bags (desktop stays `content`). readResponsive / upgradeLayout / cleanNode / sanitizeNode (each device bag through the block's own field sanitizer) / the Yjs node map (lib/editor-crdt/node-ydoc.ts) carry it, and setNodeResponsive writes it. The document is already jsonb, so no SQL. A document without the field loads and upgrades byte-identical (tested, including the frozen corpus). lib/builder/node-responsive.ts translates between the inspector's per-device values and the node (nodeDeviceValues, withDeviceValues) and resolves content for a viewport (resolveNodeContent). The canvas demo block is now a real BlockNode edited through those. Public rendering is unchanged: no public renderer reads `responsive` (test). Still open: the canvas holds its node locally and is not wired to a draft row; the inspector is not in the website or Space builder shells; an override cannot store an empty string (sanitize drops it, so it inherits); container queries on blocks and the real-viewport touch check remain a manual browser gate.

UPDATE 2026-11-16 (PROG-E5B, the canvas on a real document, dark behind EDITOR_CANVAS): /pages/canvas?space=<id or address> now reads a Space page's node document (`spaces.preferences.profileLayoutDraft`, else the published `profileLayout`; the store that already existed, no migration) behind resolveSpaceManageAccess, shows the node picked in the layer list in the inspector with fields from that block's own contract, and saves each edit to the draft only through one server action. A save carries the base the tab loaded (a counter at `preferences.profileLayoutDraftRevision` plus a document fingerprint); the counter is compared inside the single UPDATE that writes, so a stale tab conflicts and writes nothing. Nothing publishes. Two of the items above are closed: the canvas is wired to a draft, and an override can store an empty string, a default toggle or a default choice. No browser render and no real database call were made. Still open on this row: (1) a SQL function for the draft write, so it sets one key instead of the whole preferences blob and the Space page builder's saves move the same counter (a migration, so an owner decision); (2) the inspector in the website and Space builder shells; (3) inspector edits over the shared CRDT channel, so two people on one node converge; (4) rich text and image fields in the inspector (rich text shows stored markup, an image held as a library asset is kept but not drawn); (5) container queries on blocks; (6) the real-viewport, every-control-by-touch check, which needs a browser on a phone.
